shared_moves.what: Move stage_crossings (round_the_brooks, square_crossings, bridges, channel_footbridges, dike_gates) from after stage_bamboo to directly after stage_web, before stage_hinterland, in hamletgen/driver.py STAGES.
shared_moves.why: Every woods placer (village_grove's BankNear and GroveBlocks.water, the corridor keep-outs of the belt, copse, commons, woods and persimmons, bamboo_blocked, the parcels' 60 px stream keep-out) decides against the brook and the lanes as they stand; round_the_brooks fillets the brook and square_crossings rewrites lane legs AFTER all of them. Nothing between stage_web and stage_crossings adds a way or a watercourse (checked: stage_hinterland, stage_woodland, stage_windbreak, stage_bamboo write none; fixtures.py only READS lanes), so the move changes only what the woods see. round_stream's own docstring requires rounding after the ways are laid, which still holds.
shared_moves.unit_test: tests/hamletgen/test_driver (or a new test_stage_contract): over STAGES, no stage after stage_hinterland's first line writes M['streams'][*]['poly'] or M['lanes'][*]['pts'] - asserted by running each later stage's writer set from its Steps docstring against a fixed list, plus a constructed settlement where round_the_brooks is run first and a copse clump that would have crossed the fillet sliver is refused.
shared_moves.shared_with: the ways/brook area (the screen-axis brook rule and every lane-squaring rule move with it); one change, owned by whoever lands first
shared_moves.risk: medium - moves every pool map a little (the woods re-seat against the rounded brook and squared lanes); the ways are unchanged

shared_moves.what: Lift crop_to_content's frame computation (crop_boxes + CROP_MARGIN + stage_frame's extras: an outside title pocket, the confluence box, brook_beside_the_field) into one function frame_for(s, plan) and call it at the end of stage_hinterland's seating (after bamboo_seats, before the scrub pass) into plan.view; stage_frame then sets exactly plan.view, and scatter_frame / stage_windbreak's `within` read plan.view instead of re-predicting.
shared_moves.why: Three rules here are judged on meta.view (bare ground, the parcels' share inside the picture, the belt record vs ink) while their placers read a PREDICTION of it (parcels.py:275-279, stage_windbreak's _crop_boxes clamp, scatter_frame). Parity today is 'an ordering fact, not a check' (parcels.py WOODLAND_BBOX_FLOOR note) and stage_frame's extras are not in the prediction at all. With one computation there is nothing to drift.
shared_moves.later_stages: A stage after the decision that wrote a frame-setting key (Settlement._CROP_HARD, torii, fields, pond) would fall outside the view: closed by a stage-contract unit test that no stage after stage_hinterland appends to a _CROP_HARD key (bamboo_stands and bridges must be checked against _CROP_HARD when implementing; if either is frame-setting it is seated before the decision).
shared_moves.unit_test: frame_for on a constructed manifest equals crop_to_content's view; a stage-contract test as above.
shared_moves.risk: medium-high - the frame is what every pool map's composition hangs on; the title and labels still search the same window, but any map whose extras grew the frame after the scatter today will now scatter to it (that is the fix)

shared_moves.id: S3 the recorded marsh is the drawn marsh

rules.fallback: A seat outside reach is dropped; the copse is short of its area goal and meta.homestead_wood_ft2 records by how much (existing behavior). Never a clump beyond reach.

rules.rule: No copse clump's center stands inside a marsh. test_pool_261.py::test_no_copse_clump_is_based_in_the_marsh; research/vegetation.html (woody cover on the dry ground above the marsh).

rules.rule: No three woodland parcels stand in a ruled line (the third off the line through two others by less than 20% of the three's span). test_pool_261.py::test_no_three_woodland_parcels_stand_in_a_ruled_row; parcels.py:in_a_ruled_line docstring (settlement-reviews 2026-08-18, Inashiro in 261).
rows: R3 future-work/farming-communities.md 'woodland parcels in a ruled row' (Kashikawa)
rules.owner: l7r/diagram/hamletgen/hinterland/parcels.py:open_ground_patches (the accept block, 458-631) plus settlement/land/cover.py:commons (the record's x, y). Census owner correct; the record half is cover.py.
rules.mechanism: Two holes, both closed. (1) The seat is asked in_a_ruled_line only on the lattice point (seat_off_the_row, 463); the jitter (496-532) then moves it up to half a step and re-asks only _ok. Change the jitter's acceptance to `_ok(jx, jy, cand) and not in_a_ruled_line((jx, jy), centers)` (and the exclusion-radius test the lattice seat passed), so the seat appended to `centers` is always one the rule was asked of. (2) The test reads the record's x, y, which cover.py:commons writes as the RING's bbox center (cover.py:356), a third point never asked. commons takes `seat=(x, y)` from stage_woodland (plan.woodland_seats, filled beside plan.woodland_polys) and records it as the woodland parcel's x, y. The one predicate is in_a_ruled_line, asked by the placer on the recorded point, in the same order (plan order = record order).
rules.fallback: A seat whose lattice point, sideways steps and jitter all stand in a row is refused and the next scored seat is tried; with none, the map draws fewer parcels (existing documented behavior: 'the count is a target the scan meets only where there is open ground').
rules.later_stages: stage_woodland draws plan.woodland_polys in order and W13's stocking drop can remove a parcel - removing a parcel cannot create a row among the rest (a row is three parcels; a subset of row-free points is row-free under the same prefix rule only if order is kept; the drop keeps order). None else.
rules.unit_test: Constructed: two placed centers and a lattice seat off their line whose _hjit jitter would land it on the line (choose seat coordinates so the jitter lands within 20% of span) - the accepted parcel is not in a ruled line with the two; and a stub site whose only open ground is a narrow band along the crop keep-out - open_ground_patches returns at most two parcels or three off-row, and each record's x, y equals its seat.
rules.risk: low - a jitter refused or a parcel dropped on a map whose third parcel sat in a row; the record's x, y moves to the seat on every woodland parcel (any test or modal reading commons x, y for woodland must be checked)

rules.rule: Every windbreak clump inside a toe or waterside marsh is drawn as alder, and the grove's recorded alder count equals its ON-PAGE clumps in the marsh. test_pool_261.py::test_a_belt_tree_in_the_marsh_is_alder; research/vegetation.html (the marsh margin: alder or willow).
rules.owner: l7r/diagram/settlement/homestead_parts/stands.py:village_grove (the draw, 621-643) and settlement/core.py:_partition_grove_clumps (the count). Census owner correct.
rules.mechanism: The drawing is by construction (every seated clump in a wet ring is inked alder). The count breaks at set_view: `alder` counts every seated clump, the partition then moves off-page ones out of `clumps`. Record the alder clumps themselves (`alder_clumps`: the rounded seats drawn as alder) and have _partition_grove_clumps recompute g['alder'] = number of on-page clumps in alder_clumps. Decide wetness on the rounded seat so the record and the ink agree at a marsh edge. One predicate in_reed_margin(x, y, M) (role toe/waterside over marsh_ground(M), W08) read by the draw and the test.
rules.fallback: None needed - a count cannot run out of candidates.
rules.later_stages: set_view's partition - it now recounts. None else.
rules.unit_test: Constructed grove with four clumps, two in a toe ring, one of those two off the view: after set_view, alder == 1 and equals the on-page clumps in the ring; a clump 0.04 px inside the ring edge unrounded but outside when rounded is drawn and counted consistently.
rules.risk: low - record only; the ink changes at most at a marsh edge

The copse keeps the whole ring (W03). belt_polygon's `fouled` also counts a band vertex deeper than the margin, so the ladder stands the band back off the marsh as it does off the crop.

rules.later_stages: No marsh after stage_hinterland. None.

rules.rule: The marsh is subtracted from the filled dike block, the fields and the pond; it is never drawn or recorded over them (wet.py:_clipped_to_open_ground docstring; the GM's T54 complaint).
rows: R2 settlement/land/wet.py:_clip_marsh:168-183 (the function is _clipped_to_open_ground, wet.py:142-189; census name wrong)
rules.owner: l7r/diagram/settlement/land/wet.py:_clipped_to_open_ground, called from the marsh placer at wet.py:259.
rules.mechanism: Three branches return the UNCLIPPED input: a ValueError/GEOSException, an empty difference (`if not parts: return poly`), and (implicitly) an invalid input. Repair instead: make_valid/buffer(0) both the outline and each cut, retry the difference once; an empty result means the marsh has no open ground and returns None. The caller treats None as 'no marsh here' and skips the scatter and the record.
rules.fallback: The marsh is dropped (nothing drawn, nothing recorded) and meta.marsh_dropped records its role and why - never drawn over the crop.
rules.later_stages: None.
rules.unit_test: Constructed: a toe outline wholly inside a field ring -> None; a bow-tie (self-intersecting) outline laps a dike block -> a valid clipped ring outside the block; a GEOS error forced by a degenerate cut -> the retry clips or None, never the input.
retire: whatever unit test pins the 'falls back to the input' branch of _clipped_to_open_ground (grep tests for _clipped_to_open_ground when implementing)
rules.risk: low - the branch is rare (census: degenerate outline / GEOS exception)

rules.rule: The marsh's recorded outline is the ground its reeds are drawn on, so every rule that asks 'is this in the marsh' asks the drawn marsh (R3: marshes[0].poly keeps ground the scatter left dry).
rows: R3 future-work/farming-communities.md 'The toe marsh's recorded outline is not the drawn marsh' - its first half

rules.mechanism: The scatter refuses fields (+10 px), block_polys, clearings, `avoid` and corridors inside the outline (wet.py:318-326) while the record keeps the whole ring. Record the drawn ground: the outline minus the scatter's AREA keep-outs (fields padded 10, block_polys, clearings, avoid; corridors are threads and stay) through the same shapely path _clipped_to_open_ground uses, keyholed to one ring (_keyholed). One predicate marsh_ground(M) -> rings, read by GroveBlocks (W03, W06), W05's in_reed_margin, parcels' wet test (W12), belt_polygon's _in_marsh and trim_off_marsh.

rules.later_stages: A clearing reserved after the marsh (farmstead_fixtures' household shrines run after s.hinterland(commons=False)) would make the record over-claim again - closed by W10's ordering (clearings reserved before the scatter).

rules.rule: A way does not run into a reed bed: neither end stands on the marsh (wet.py:trim_off_marsh docstring, GM 2026-08-12).
rules.owner: l7r/diagram/settlement/land/wet.py:trim_off_marsh; callers hamletgen/ways/web.py:196 (arms), hamletgen/ways/track.py:473 (the field spur), settlement/rolling/roll.py:311 (legacy tier, out of scope).
rules.mechanism: When the last remaining leg of a two-point way is wholly wet (d <= 30 px with nothing left to pop), the loop `break`s and ships the soaked end. Return [] instead: a way wholly on the marsh is no way. web.py and track.py already handle an empty arm/spur as 'nowhere to go' (test_lane_clipping states that drop) - confirm at implementation; the reach of every farmhouse is the ways area's guarantee, not this one.
rules.fallback: The way is dropped and the caller's own no-way path runs.
rules.later_stages: The toe marsh is laid after the web, so the web trims only against marshes known then (pond fringe, waterward); a way ending where the toe is later laid is the ways area's toe_band prediction (wet.py:toe_band), not this function.
rules.unit_test: trim_off_marsh on a two-point way lying inside a marsh ring -> []; on a way with one wet end -> the wet end walked back to dry ground.
retire: any test pinning the shortened-soaked-leg result (grep tests for trim_off_marsh)
rules.risk: low - rare branch; the drop is coordinated with the ways area

rules.rule: Ground cover (commons scrub, marsh reeds) is never drawn over a swept clearing, nor its record over a feature its class may not overlap. tests/gate/test_no_feature_overlaps.py::test_the_ground_cover_scatter_respects_what_was_swept_before_it; cover.py module docstring.
rules.owner: l7r/diagram/hamletgen/hinterland/stages.py:stage_hinterland (the order) and settlement/land/cover.py:_clear_ground (the registry). Census owner correct for the order.
rules.mechanism: The scatter skips only clearings that exist when it runs, and farmstead_fixtures (household shrines, which reserve clearings) runs after the marsh pass (stages.py:82 then 86). Two parts. (1) Order: split the fixtures' clearing reservations out of farmstead_fixtures into a reserve step run before s.hinterland(commons=False) - the fixtures' seats depend on the marsh only for the persimmons' trunk test, which stays where it is. (2) Structural backstop so order cannot matter: the scatter's marks and blades are already deferred to finish (_mark_groups, _blade_groups); the flush culls every mark and blade whose base lies in any clearing ring (one predicate: the KeepoutGrid ring hit over self.clearings the scatter itself uses), and _clear_ground records the clearing's seq so a clearing reserved after a scatter is also subtracted from that cover's recorded poly (keyholed). The matrix pairs (commons/marshes vs a forbidden class) are asked with overlap/taxonomy's own pair table at record time: the cover record is the scatter ring minus every forbidden-class footprint present, and a later placer seating a forbidden class tests its footprint (not its center) against cover records via block_polys.
rules.fallback: Cover marks inside a clearing are removed (the clearing is bare, which is what it is); no feature moves.
rules.later_stages: Any clearing reserved after the scatter - covered by the flush cull, which runs last.
rules.unit_test: Constructed: a commons scattered over a square, then reserve_clearing inside it - after finish, no blade or mark base inside the clearing and the recorded commons ring excludes it; the same with a marsh.
retire: tests/gate/test_no_feature_overlaps.py::test_the_ground_cover_scatter_respects_what_was_swept_before_it (the `comb` roll it needs, if no other test reads it)
rules.risk: medium - touches the finish flush every map runs through; the ink changes only where a clearing lies under cover

rules.rule: No more than 35% of the rendered view is ground that no cover, field or built footprint covers - between the fields and the settlement there is always something (margins_form_continuous_ring). tests/gate/test_crossings_and_cover.py::test_the_countryside_has_no_holes_in_it.
rules.owner: l7r/diagram/settlement/land/cover.py:hinterland (the composer that lays the ring strips and interior fill), driven from hamletgen/hinterland/stages.py:stage_hinterland. Census owner correct.
rules.mechanism: Lift the test's measure into the engine as bare_cells(M, view, step=25) (cover.py) - the one predicate - reading the same cover keys, footprints and pond. With the view decided once (S2), stage_hinterland's second hinterland() call, after the scrub, asks bare_cells over plan.view counting the woodland parcels and the belt band already planned (plan.woodland_polys, plan.belt) as cover, and while the bare share exceeds the bar lays a grazing commons over the largest connected block of bare cells (a ring of those cells, clipped to the scatter keep-outs as every commons is). FR-003 correction to the predicate: the test counts a lane, a stream, a well, a clearing or a burial ground as bare; those are 'something' by the rule's own words, so bare_cells counts every recorded footprint and tread as covered, and the retired test with it.
rules.fallback: A bare cell that no commons may cover under the overlap rules is by construction a cell some recorded feature occupies, which the corrected predicate counts as covered - so the fill always has somewhere to go. If after corrections the bar still cannot be met, see impossible[0].
rules.later_stages: stage_woodland, stage_windbreak and stage_bamboo only ADD cover. stage_frame's crop - closed by S2 (the view is the one the fill measured). The scatter frame (scatter_frame) must contain plan.view or the scrub stops short of the page (its own docstring): S2 derives it from plan.view.
rules.unit_test: Constructed settlement with a field in the middle of a view and no ring strip on two sides: after stage_hinterland's cover pass, bare_cells over the view <= 35%; a view where lanes and a clearing fill 20% counts them covered.
rules.risk: medium - the fill fires rarely (the pool passes today), but S2 is a prerequisite and moves the frame logic

rules.rule: A woodland commons parcel never stands more than half in marsh (5x5 samples over its drawn ring's bbox). tests/gate/test_settlement_cover.py::test_a_woodland_commons_stands_on_dry_ground.
rules.owner: l7r/diagram/hamletgen/hinterland/parcels.py:open_ground_patches (_wet, parcels.py:243-244). Census owner correct.

One predicate parcel_wet_share(ring, marsh_ground(M)) in parcels.py, the test's 5x5; the accept block asks it on the ring _parcel_outline returns (the ring is built before `chosen.append`, so the refusal costs nothing) and refuses a share > 12/25. Keep the 3x3 scan probe as the cheap prefilter.
rules.fallback: The seat is refused and the next scored seat tried; fewer parcels.
rules.later_stages: No marsh after stage_hinterland. None.
rules.unit_test: A constructed marsh finger threading between the 3x3 probes of a seat, covering 14 of the ring's 25 samples: the seat is refused.

rules.rule: A woodland commons parcel never records fewer than 5 crowns. tests/gate/test_settlement_cover.py::test_a_woodland_commons_is_visibly_stocked.
rules.owner: l7r/diagram/settlement/land/cover.py:commons (role='woodland', 235-280), with hamletgen/hinterland/parcels.py:open_ground_patches offering the parcel. Census owner correct.
rules.mechanism: commons throws _wd_target*6 random points and records whatever count results. Lift woodland_crown_seats(s, ring) (the _sparse keep-outs + CrownIndex, deterministic grid at COMMONS_SPACING_FT after the random throws) into cover.py; open_ground_patches asks it on the drawn ring before accepting and refuses a parcel under MIN_CROWNS (moved into the engine beside COMMONS_SPACING_FT, the test's 5). Everything the commons keep-out reads (fields, block_polys, clearings, corridors, water, halo, existing tree_crowns) exists at scan time. commons then fills the parcel with the same function, so the count it records is at least the count the scan saw.
rules.fallback: The parcel is not offered; the scan takes the next seat; fewer parcels.
rules.later_stages: Crowns written between the scan and stage_woodland (persimmons in farmstead_fixtures, household bamboo) could take seats the scan counted - the parcel keeps them out by the scan's keep (houses at 150 px) so they cannot reach it; asserted in the unit test by a fixture seat at the keep's edge.

retire: the `woodland` fixture's fallback to a pool manifest when the roll loses its woodland (census note), if nothing else reads it

rules.rule: A woodland commons parcel's drawn ring keeps at least 70% of its bbox inside the rendered view. tests/gate/test_settlement_cover.py::test_a_woodland_commons_is_mostly_inside_the_picture.
rules.owner: l7r/diagram/hamletgen/hinterland/parcels.py:open_ground_patches (parcel_bbox_ok, 52-75). Census owner correct.
rules.mechanism: Two mismatches. (1) parcel_bbox_ok measures the rotated RECTANGLE's bbox; the test measures the drawn RING's bbox, and the ring (0.80-1.00 of the inscribed ellipse) has a different bbox and share. One predicate parcel_inside_share(ring, frame) - the test's formula - asked on the ring from _parcel_outline before acceptance, at WOODLAND_BBOX_FLOOR. (2) The frame is a prediction; with S2 the frame asked at scan time is contained in plan.view (crop boxes are only appended after the scan, and S2 sets the view from the same function), and the share inside a larger frame is never smaller.
rules.fallback: fit_square_parcel's shrink ladder, then the seat is dropped (existing).
rules.later_stages: stage_frame's crop - closed by S2.
rules.unit_test: A constructed seat whose rotated rect sits 73% inside the frame but whose ring bbox sits 68% inside: refused; and a parcel accepted at scan time whose frame is then grown - share never falls.
rules.risk: low

rules.rule: A recorded village grove never holds fewer than 1.5 clumps per 100k sq px of its recorded w x h. tests/gate/test_settlement_cover.py::test_every_recorded_grove_holds_trees.
rules.owner: l7r/diagram/settlement/homestead_parts/stands.py:village_grove (the record, 646-687). Census note partly wrong: the COPSE already records its clumps' extent (stands.py:663-669); only the windbreak records the requested polygon.

Copse: after seating, while the record fails it, drop the clump farthest from the clumps' centroid and re-derive the extent - terminates, since one clump's extent (clump + 8 px square) is far above the floor. rules.mechanism: Lift belt_depths (test_pool_wind.py:85-158) into belt.py as the one predicate, taking the view from plan.view (S2) and the lanes/brook as they stand (S1). village_grove(role='windbreak') gets a depth pass after the gap fill: for each bin reading < 30 ft, offer that column the gap fill's depth search (the band's own depth at the column, middle outward, static_clear and near_seats) until the bin reaches 30 ft. Where the column's plantable depth inside the band is under 30 ft (a plot, a sun lane or a crop inside the band), the band is pushed back for that column: belt_polygon takes a per-column `back` (it already has a global one, belt.py:334) and stage_windbreak re-lays that stretch of the band and re-seats it, up to the ladder's 60 ft.
rules.fallback: A column that no push-back within 60 ft can deepen to 30 ft (the crop or the page bounds it) ends the belt run there: the belt is recorded as runs, and that stretch is a declared break (meta.belt_breaks with its cause) that W17 treats as a run end. GM-QUESTION: the research says a hole funnels the wind and the one attested opening is an angled crossing; it is silent on what a planted belt did where the ground ahead of it is field or water - a thinner belt there (breaks this rule) or a break (breaks continuity) are distinct forms.

rules.rule: The windbreak's drawn center stands within 45 degrees of northwest of the cluster center, and its crowns subtend no more than 200 degrees round it (a hook on one or two sides). tests/hamletgen/test_pool_wind.py::test_every_pool_hamlet_has_its_belt_on_the_regional_northwest; research/vegetation 'Does a shelter belt wrap the settlement?'.
rules.owner: l7r/diagram/settlement/homestead_parts/stands.py:village_grove (the drawn clumps the rule measures) and hamletgen/hinterland/belt.py:belt_polygon (the band). The household-count assertion bundled in the same test (len(houses) == households) belongs to stage_homesteads' seat placer - split out to the homesteads/seating area.
rules.mechanism: One predicate belt_bearing_and_subtense(clumps, houses) lifted from the test. Constrain then repair: (1) belt_polygon floors each column at max(median u, 0) instead of median u (belt.py:254-255), so the band's centroid is strictly windward of the house centroid (u > 36 ft); with the wind the regional NW (meta written unconditionally in skeleton.py) a band symmetric across the wind then bears within 45 deg by construction. (2) After seating and W16/W17, if the drawn clumps' subtense exceeds 200 deg, trim clumps from the belt's ends (the runs' extreme angular crowns) until it does not; if the bearing is off, trim the heavier arm's end. Each trim removes an END clump, so W16/W17 are untouched in the runs that remain.
rules.fallback: Trimming converges: removing end crowns drives the centroid toward the band's middle, which (1) puts windward of the cluster; at worst the belt is its middle stretch.
rules.later_stages: set_view's partition does not move clumps (the test reads on-page clumps: the trim must read what is on the page - with S2 the view is known when village_grove runs, so the predicate is asked on the clumps inside plan.view).
rules.unit_test: A constructed cluster lying diagonally to the wind with its median house downwind of the centroid: the recorded belt bears within 45 deg of NW; a cluster the band wraps on three sides: subtense <= 200 deg after the trim.
retire: tests/hamletgen/test_pool_wind.py::test_every_pool_hamlet_has_its_belt_on_the_regional_northwest - its meta and belt halves; the households half moves to the seating area's placer test
rules.risk: high - the belt's position is its meaning; clamping the polygon to move its center was tried and walked cohort seeds 19 and 28 to the lee side (stages.py:206-212); the floor change moves every belt whose median house sits upwind of the centroid

rules.rule: The windbreak shelters houses: no belt crown stands farther from every farmhouse than the band's own designed far face (near 36 + depth 100 + far rag 10 + sun offset + back); a stretch with no house before it is not planted (belt_polygon docstring; Inashiro 63 of 308 crowns over 200 ft from any house, furthest 518).
rows: R3 future-work/farming-communities.md '## The windbreak's far limb, where a cluster sits in two groups'
rules.owner: l7r/diagram/hamletgen/hinterland/belt.py:fringe_profile (a column with no house leans on its neighbor, belt.py:57-60) and the shoulder `half + 90` (207); village_grove refuses by reach.
rules.mechanism: belt_polygon computes and records the band's far-face reach R (the sum above, per map). village_grove(role='windbreak') takes near=(houses, R) through the same Seats index the copse uses, so a clump beyond R of every house is refused on every seat path including the gap fill (which already asks _near, stands.py:569). fringe_profile marks columns with no house within `wide` as empty; W17's belt_gaps treats an empty-column stretch as a run end, so a split cluster gets two runs rather than a limb joining them.
rules.fallback: Clumps past the reach are not seated; the belt is shorter or in two runs.
rules.later_stages: None - houses are final before the belt.
rules.unit_test: A constructed cluster in two groups 500 ft apart across the wind: no recorded crown beyond R of a house, and the belt is two runs with no crowns between them.
rules.risk: medium - shortens belts with a shoulder or a split cluster (Inashiro); interacts with W16/W17's run handling

rules.mechanism: One predicate reads_as_a_disc(ring) (radius coefficient of variation under a threshold and no straight run). _parcel_outline clips its ellipse by the nearest bounding line within reach - a lane's or the brook's keep-out, the crop set-back - where one lies within the tested reach, and roughens the rest; the accept block refuses a ring the predicate reads as a disc and re-rolls the harmonics from the next seed offset.
rules.fallback: A lot with no bounding line in reach keeps the roughened ellipse with a larger harmonic amplitude until the predicate passes (the amplitude is a calibrated degree, bounded by the tested reach).
rules.later_stages: None.

impossible.rule: W11 - at most 35% bare ground in the view

As the retired test reads it (lanes, streams, clearings, burial grounds counted bare) a view those features fill past 35% cannot be covered without laying cover over features the overlap matrix forbids it. For review: adopt the corrected predicate, which is the rule's own grounding ('a margin grass, scrub, a grazing common, a marsh, a wood, a yard').

impossible.rule: W25 - every homestead's drawn wood at least 6,000 sq ft
impossible.reason: Where the ground in reach of the homesteads and in the belt's lee is already taken (Kuwabata's single row on a dike head: crops, water and the dike on every side), no placer can draw the floor without widening the copse's reach past what research/vegetation/210's 'among the houses' allows or seating wood beyond the frame. For review: accept a recorded shortfall on such a site, or change the siting rule.

impossible.rule: R3 'Two checks that pass VACUOUSLY - woodland': every roll draws at least one woodland parcel (Sawada and Kashikawa roll zero)
impossible.reason: The scan already relaxes set-back, size and aspect before dropping; what is left on those maps is that no legal ground lies inside the tight frame (the GM's frame rule: the commons never set it). A village's wood on the nearest hill beyond the fields (research/vegetation/220) can lie off the sheet; guaranteeing one ON it means letting a parcel set the frame or drawing it under the floor or on the crop's set-back - a change to what the feature is. For review: record meta.woodland_offsheet with a bearing, or let one parcel set the frame (GM-QUESTION: distinct forms, research silent on whether the sheet must show it).

impossible.reason: Not impossible, but the fallback is a choice between two forms the research does not decide (a thinner belt there vs a recorded break in it); listed so the GM rules before implementation rather than after.
